high.title: Household Deposits Exceed 10.5 Million Billion VND, Setting New Record
high.summary: According to newly released data from the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), household deposits in the banking system reached over 10.56 million billion VND by end-March 2026, up 2.19% from end-2025. This represents a record high for Vietnamese household savings. In contrast, corporate and economic organization deposits fell 2.69% to over 6 million billion VND, reflecting businesses' capital usage needs for production and investment activities in early 2026. Households added approximately 200,000 billion VND to the banking system in Q1/2026 alone, with year-over-year growth exceeding 3 million billion VND. This trend continues the multi-year pattern of idle household funds flowing to banks as a key savings and asset preservation channel. The sustained growth in household deposits demonstrates banks remain the preferred savings destination, providing stable funding sources for credit growth while reflecting Vietnamese citizens' conservative investment approach and trust in the banking system.

high.title: Developing Capital Markets to "Share the Burden" with Banking System
high.summary: Vietnam's ambitious GDP growth target of over 10% annually during 2026-2030 requires massive medium and long-term capital for infrastructure, energy, digital transformation, and green transition investments. With bank credit remaining the economy's primary funding channel, developing capital markets to share the burden with the banking system has become increasingly urgent. According to BIDV Deputy CEO Doan Viet Nam, 2026 alone requires 4.9-5 million billion VND in capital (equivalent to 33-33.7% of GDP). Key sectors like infrastructure, energy, and digital transformation involve projects worth tens of thousands of billions VND with long investment cycles. This development imperative highlights the need for robust bond markets and equity financing to complement traditional bank lending, reducing systemic risk concentration in the banking sector while providing more diverse funding sources for Vietnam's growth ambitions.

high.title: Savings Interest Rates June 12 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary: Survey of online deposit rates at major banks on June 12 shows interest rates remain stable across the system. State-owned banks maintain their maximum rate of 6.8% annually, while many commercial joint-stock banks apply 6.9-7% for long-term deposits. Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank and VietinBank continue offering identical rate structures: 1-month and 3-month terms at 4.75%; 6-month and 9-month at 6.6%; 12-18 month terms at 6.8%. MBV and VCBNeo lead the market with 7% rates for 6-18 month terms. The stable rate environment suggests SBV policy effectiveness in managing liquidity and inflation expectations, while providing banks adequate funding costs for lending operations. The convergence of rates among state banks indicates coordinated monetary policy implementation, supporting VND stability and economic growth objectives.

medium.title: Payment Security: The "Race Without Finish Line" for the Banking Industry
medium.summary: Vietnam Banking Association organized the 2026 Payment Risk Management Conference in Ninh Binh on June 12, themed "Payment Security in the Digital Era: Opportunities and Challenges." Dr. Dao Minh Tu emphasized that payment security is no longer individual banks' responsibility but a strategic task ensuring system-wide sustainable development, directly affecting market confidence and requiring continuous technology infrastructure investment.

medium.title: Gold Prices Hit Week's High on June 13 Evening
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices continued rising strongly on June 13, reaching the week's highest levels. SJC quoted plain gold rings at 143.9-146.9 million VND/tael and gold bars at 144-147 million VND/tael, both up 1.6 million VND/tael from the previous session. Other major dealers like PNJ, DOJI, and Bao Tin Minh Chau reported similar increases.

medium.title: Gold Plunged 49 Million VND/Tael from Peak, Seafood Company Benefits Nearly 285 Billion VND
medium.summary: SJC gold prices fell from peaks of 191.3 million VND/tael to around 142.4 million VND/tael on June 12, representing a 48.9 million VND decline (nearly 26%). This benefits APT seafood company, which has outstanding gold-denominated debt of 5,833 taels from a 2009 loan, as the debt's VND value decreases with falling gold prices.

medium.title: One Bank to Pay 7.5% Dividend, Rights Record Date in June
medium.summary: Bac A Bank announced June 26, 2026 as the record date for stock dividend rights at 7.5% ratio. The bank plans to issue over 80.4 million shares worth more than 804 billion VND, using undistributed retained earnings from 2025. Charter capital will increase from over 10.721 trillion VND to approximately 11.525 trillion VND post-issuance.
